passage_notes.gist: This passage establishes Della's poverty on Christmas Eve and her loving desperation to buy a worthy present for Jim.
This passage introduces the couple's two prized possessions and shows Della revealing her magnificent hair before rushing out to the street with a sudden resolve.
Della sells her long hair for twenty dollars to buy a platinum fob chain for Jim's watch, then hurries home to curl her shorn hair.
Della anxiously awaits Jim with his gift, and when he arrives and stares unreadably at her shorn hair, she explains she sold it to buy his Christmas present.
Jim struggles to absorb Della's sacrifice, reassures her his love is unchanged, and gives her a package whose opening swings her from ecstatic joy to tears.
The passage reveals Jim sold his watch to buy Della's now-unusable combs and closes by declaring their foolish mutual sacrifice the wisest giving of all.
